x: FDI is a mostly non-debt capital flow that brings long-term foreign investment into Indian enterprises. Volatile investment in securities is FPI.
Option B is incorrect: FDI is more stable and long-term than portfolio investment, while FPI is the more volatile one. FDI also brings technology and skills.
Both are true: FDI is long-term investment in Indian enterprises because it is stable and lasting compared with portfolio flows. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the nature explains the role.

x: FDI brings more control and technology and skills, while FPI is mainly financial capital and more volatile. Because both appear twice, the answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.

I, III and IV are correct: FDI can come through shares, debentures, preference shares and warrants, and is allowed in e-commerce marketplaces but not inventory models. II is false because the automatic route needs no prior approval.
t: Discriminate the automatic route from the government route.

x: FDI stands for Foreign Direct Investment. FPI is Foreign Portfolio Investment.
All four are correct: FDI is linked with innovation, competition, jobs and export competitiveness.
Foreign subsidiaries, majority foreign holdings and wholly foreign-funded companies count as FDI. Portfolio investment does not count as FDI automatically. The answer is a-i, b-i, c-i, d-ii.
FII is mainly financial capital invested in securities markets. FDI brings capital along with technology and management.
Option C is incorrect: SEBI's FPI Regulations, 2019, brought FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs together under the FPI framework.
Both are true: a P-Note gives an overseas investor exposure to Indian shares without SEBI registration, because a registered FII/FPI issues it to them. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the issuer explains the access.

x: FII is mainly financial capital and more volatile, while FDI brings capital with technology and management and is less volatile. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
Both are true: FII is short-term and buoyant, while FDI is stable and long-term.
FII stands for Foreign Institutional Investor, now covered under the FPI framework.
I and II are correct: FDI is direct investment in enterprises or sectors. III is false because FII is portfolio investment, not direct investment.
Option C is incorrect: masala bonds are issued abroad but in Indian rupees. The first was issued by the IFC in November 2014.
The IFC was set up in 1956 and the IDA in 1960. The IFC focuses on the private sector, and the IDA gives soft loans and grants. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Discriminate the IFC from the IDA.

x: All three are correct: the first masala bond was issued abroad, in rupees, to fund Indian infrastructure.
Both are true: the IFC is an international development institution and part of the World Bank Group. Group membership does not explain its nature, so R does not explain A.
Both are true: the IDA belongs to the World Bank Group and lends to the poorest countries on soft terms.
